answer: Step Marks \(F(s) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) e^{isx} dx = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-a}^{a} e^{isx} dx\) (2) \(= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \left[ \frac{e^{isx}}{is} \right]_{-a}^{a} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cdot \frac{e^{isa} - e^{-isa}}{is}\) (3) \(= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cdot \frac{2i \sin(as)}{is} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \cdot \frac{\sin(as)}{s}\) (3) For \(s = 0\): \(F(0) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{-a}^{a} dx = \frac{2a}{\sqrt{2\pi}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} a\) (2)
